title: InSeasonOpportunityRecord
description: One player on the in-season Opportunity Board: the intrinsic rest-of-season estimate beside documented fantasy-market BEHAVIOUR. The behaviour signals are add and drop counts over a declared lookback window from a declared snapshot - they are not a price, not an ADP, not a rank, and no field here is subtracted from a rank (roadmap 10.3, 12.3). Behaviour may decide whether a player is surfaced; it may never change a single intrinsic number, and the artifact carries the intrinsic values unmodified from ros_tiers.json so that is checkable rather than promised.

behavior_source_id.description: Which behaviour feed supplied the counts. `sleeper` in Release 2.

behavior_available.description: False when the optional behaviour capture was unavailable or stale. The board still publishes every intrinsic number: a failed behaviour source degrades this column, never the rest-of-season estimate (roadmap 12.5).

behavior_snapshot_at_utc.description: When the snapshot was taken. Sleeper publishes no observation time of its own, so this is the retrieval time and is recorded as such rather than presented as a data-as-of claim.

behavior_lookback_hours.description: The lookback window REQUESTED. Sleeper publishes nothing about the window it actually used, so the record describes the request (ADR-062's discipline, applied to behaviour).

behavior_request_limit.description: The row limit requested. A player absent from a top-N feed has count 0 for that feed and is not missing data.

add_count.description: Rosters that added this player inside the lookback window. A count of transactions, in transactions. Never a pick number and never converted into one.

net_add_count.description: add_count minus drop_count. Both sides are the same unit measured over the same window by the same feed, which is the only reason this subtraction is legitimate.

add_rank.description: This player's position in the add feed, 1 being the most added. An ordering of the behaviour feed itself; it is not a draft rank and is never differenced against `ros_fair_rank`.

snap_share_last3.description: Recent share of team offensive snaps: the role context that makes a promotion visible. A model input as well as context, and shown as such.

current_status.description: Current roster status. Annotation only, visually separate from every model input, and never a model feature.

surface_reasons.description: Why this player is visible: inside the intrinsic depth, or surfaced by current role/behaviour evidence. A surfaced player carries a fair rank the model computed and no tier.
